layered_rice.instruction: Cook and drain sliced shiitake separately, then scatter them over the rice layer.
layered_rice.reason: Seasoned mushrooms add a Japanese-inspired rice topping while keeping the original layers and moisture balance.

rice.instruction: Cook sliced shiitake separately and serve them over the prepared rice.
rice.reason: The shiitake topping draws on Japanese mixed-rice recipes and preserves the source rice method.

simmered.instruction: Whisk a little miso into a small amount of the cooked sauce and stir it back in off the heat. Taste before adding more.
simmered.reason: Miso adds a savory accent to the existing sauce, while the original sauce and main ingredient still lead.

wet_heat.instruction: For a savory broth, try a small splash of unsalted kombu and shiitake dashi in one serving before seasoning.
wet_heat.reason: A small trial portion gives a Japanese-inspired broth accent without changing the cooking method.

roasted.instruction: Thin a little miso with water and brush a small amount onto a cooked portion just before serving.
roasted.reason: A thin miso finish draws on dengaku and leaves the original roasting, grilling or frying step intact.

sweet.instruction: Try a light dusting of unsweetened kinako (roasted soybean flour) on one finished serving.
sweet.reason: A roasted-soy finish adds a Japanese-inspired accent without changing dough, batter, sweetness or setting ratios.

finish.instruction: Taste a small serving with a light drizzle of miso loosened with water and adjust before seasoning the rest.
finish.reason: A tasting portion keeps the source recipe intact while testing a Japanese-style miso accent.

rice.ingredients: toasted sesame oil and roasted gim
rice.instruction: Add toasted sesame oil and crushed roasted gim to a cooked rice portion just before serving.
rice.reason: The sesame and seaweed finish adds aroma without changing the rice water or cooking time.

simmered.instruction: Dissolve a little doenjang in a spoonful of the cooked stew. Stir it back into one serving off the heat and finish with sliced scallion.
simmered.reason: Fermented soybean paste adds savory depth to the existing broth or sauce.

roasted.ingredients: gochujang, toasted sesame oil and rice vinegar
roasted.instruction: Stir gochujang, sesame oil and rice vinegar into a thin glaze. Brush it onto the cooked portion just before serving.
roasted.reason: The sweet-spicy glaze accents the original char and stays away from direct heat.

sweet.ingredients: roasted soybean powder and toasted sesame
sweet.instruction: Dust one finished serving with roasted soybean powder and toasted sesame just before serving.
sweet.reason: An injeolmi-inspired finish adds nuttiness while preserving the original batter or filling.

finish.ingredients: toasted sesame oil, scallion and roasted sesame
finish.instruction: Finish one serving with a little sesame oil, sliced scallion and roasted sesame.
finish.reason: The toasted and fresh aromatics build a Korean-inspired accent over the existing seasoning.

rice.ingredients: crispy shallots, lime zest and Thai basil
rice.instruction: Finish cooked rice with crispy shallots, a little lime zest and torn Thai basil.
rice.reason: The shallots and herbs add contrast while keeping the rice texture and liquid ratio.

simmered.instruction: Steep bruised lemongrass and makrut lime leaf in a small ladleful of the cooked sauce, strain, then stir back a little before serving.
simmered.reason: Infusing a small portion adds citrus aroma while keeping the original broth or sauce.

roasted.ingredients: lime juice, bird’s-eye chile and cilantro
roasted.instruction: Mix lime juice, a little minced chile and cilantro. Spoon over the cooked portion when serving.
roasted.reason: A fresh chile-lime dressing contrasts with a grilled or roasted surface.

sweet.instruction: Spoon a little coconut cream over one finished serving and add toasted coconut.
sweet.reason: The coconut topping adds richness outside the original batter or setting mixture.

finish.ingredients: lime, Thai basil and crispy shallots
finish.instruction: Add a squeeze of lime, torn Thai basil and crispy shallots just before serving.
finish.reason: This finish adds acidity, aroma and crunch to the existing dish.

rice.instruction: Fold finely diced roasted poblano and chopped cilantro into cooked rice at serving, or scatter them over a layered rice portion.
rice.reason: A roasted chile and herb finish preserves the original grains and layers.

simmered.ingredients: ancho chile, Mexican oregano and lime
simmered.instruction: Soften a pinch of ground ancho chile and Mexican oregano in a spoonful of the cooked sauce over low heat. Stir it into one portion and finish with a little lime off the heat.
simmered.reason: Ancho and oregano deepen the existing sauce while lime brightens the finish.

roasted.instruction: Mix softened guajillo chile with garlic and lime into a thin dressing. Brush or spoon it onto the cooked portion just before serving.
roasted.reason: A guajillo-lime finish adds chile depth without disturbing the original char.

sweet.instruction: Add a light dusting of Mexican cinnamon and toasted pepitas to one finished serving.
sweet.reason: Warm spice and crunch sit on top of the dessert without changing its structure.

finish.ingredients: lime, cilantro and pickled red onion
finish.instruction: Top one serving with chopped cilantro and pickled red onion, then add lime to taste.
finish.reason: The fresh and pickled accents lift the original seasoning.

rice.ingredients: lemon zest, parsley and extra-virgin olive oil
rice.instruction: Fold chopped parsley, a little lemon zest and olive oil into a cooked rice portion or scatter them over a layered portion.
rice.reason: The herb-and-citrus finish preserves the original rice method.

simmered.ingredients: basil, extra-virgin olive oil and cracked black pepper
simmered.instruction: Stir torn basil into one portion of the finished sauce off the heat, then finish with olive oil and cracked black pepper.
simmered.reason: Fresh basil and olive oil complement the sauce while preserving its original reduction and spices.

roasted.instruction: Warm chopped rosemary and garlic in a little olive oil, remove from the heat and add lemon zest. Brush onto the cooked portion at serving.
roasted.reason: The rosemary-garlic oil complements browning and adds aroma after cooking.

sweet.ingredients: orange zest and shaved dark chocolate
sweet.instruction: Finish one serving with orange zest and shaved dark chocolate just before serving.
sweet.reason: The citrus and chocolate topping leaves the original sweetness and setting ratios intact.

finish.ingredients: flat-leaf parsley, lemon zest and garlic
finish.instruction: Chop parsley with lemon zest and a little garlic and sprinkle over one serving just before eating.
finish.reason: A gremolata-inspired finish adds a bright herbal accent without changing the original spice base.

rice.instruction: Scatter toasted pine nuts and chopped dill over cooked rice just before serving.
rice.reason: This topping adds a pilaf-inspired nutty finish and keeps the original grains intact.

simmered.ingredients: Aleppo pepper, dried mint and butter
simmered.instruction: Briefly warm Aleppo pepper and dried mint in a little melted butter and drizzle over one serving of the cooked stew or soup.
simmered.reason: A spiced butter finish perfumes the original broth or sauce.

roasted.instruction: Toss thinly sliced red onion and parsley with sumac and serve alongside the cooked portion.
roasted.reason: The tang and crunch complement the existing grilled or roasted flavors.

sweet.instruction: Perfume a spoonful of the recipe’s existing sauce with a drop of food-grade orange blossom water and add crushed pistachios at serving. Use the pistachios alone if there is no sauce.
sweet.reason: The finishing aroma and crunch leave the original dessert method intact.

finish.instruction: Finish a tasting portion with sumac, chopped parsley and a little olive oil.
finish.reason: The tart and herbal finish accents the source seasoning.

rice.ingredients: fried onions, ghee and green chile
rice.instruction: Top cooked rice with fried onions and sliced green chile, and drizzle a little warm ghee just before serving.
rice.reason: The aromatic finish complements layered rice and preserves the source method.

simmered.ingredients: panch phoron, dried red chile and mustard oil
simmered.instruction: Briefly bloom panch phoron and dried red chile in a little culinary mustard oil. Spoon the tempering over one portion of the cooked stew or dal.
simmered.reason: The finishing tempering adds whole-spice aroma to the existing sauce or lentils.

roasted.ingredients: roasted cumin, green chile and lime
roasted.instruction: Mix roasted ground cumin, minced green chile and lime. Spoon a little over the cooked portion just before serving.
roasted.reason: A cumin-chile-lime finish complements the existing browning and spice paste.

sweet.ingredients: date palm jaggery and toasted coconut
sweet.instruction: Add a few shavings of date palm jaggery and toasted coconut to one portion at serving.
sweet.reason: A pitha-inspired finish adds caramel and coconut notes without changing the original batter or filling.

finish.ingredients: green chile, cilantro and mustard oil
finish.instruction: Add minced green chile, cilantro and a small drizzle of culinary mustard oil to one serving.
finish.reason: The fresh aromatics and pungent oil build a Bangladeshi-inspired finishing accent.
